intro: A plumbing leak left unattended can cause water damage to floorboards, plasterboard ceilings, and electrical circuits within hours. FixWell Services carries out plumbing repairs across Salisbury and Wiltshire, isolating the leak source, making the correct repair to copper or plastic pipework, and preventing secondary water damage. For active bursts, our emergency handyman service provides same-day attendance. Call us on +44 7391 599 078 for same-day emergency attendance or use the quote form to book a routine repair.

sections.heading: What Plumbing Leak Repair Involves
sections.body: A plumbing leak is any unintended release of water from the pressurised supply system or the gravity-fed waste system. In Salisbury's housing stock (which ranges from Victorian terraces with original 15mm copper pipework to 1990s new-builds fitted with plastic pushfit systems) leaks arise from several distinct failure points. Compression joints fail when an olive deforms or a nut works loose from vibration. Solder/capillary joints on copper pipework can develop pinholes from corrosion, particularly in homes with aggressive water chemistry. Pushfit fittings (Speedfit, JG Layflat) can release from the pipe if the insert collet is damaged or if the pipe was not fully inserted. Threaded BSP connections on valves and stopcocks leak when PTFE tape deteriorates or a fibre washer hardens with age. Identifying the exact joint type, pipe material, and access constraints is the first step before any repair is attempted.

sections.heading: Common Leak Locations and Failure Causes
sections.body: The most frequent leak locations we attend in Salisbury homes are under-sink supply flexibles (braided hose connectors that fatigue and split at the olive end), radiator valve spindles (older TRVs and wheelhead valves develop spindle seal wear), and stopcocks under kitchen sinks that have not been turned for years and develop body leaks when finally operated. In Victorian and Edwardian terraces across St Ann Street, Fisherton Street, and the Friary Estate, original lead pipework occasionally surfaces, typically on the cold feed from the street main, and requires careful assessment before repair. Pinhole corrosion in 15mm copper is common in properties where aggressive water treatment or electrolytic action between copper and steel components has occurred. Each failure mode requires a different repair approach: olive replacement, pipe section cutting and re-joining, valve cartridge swap, or full pipe reroute where access is too restricted.

sections.heading: How FixWell Diagnoses and Repairs Leaks
sections.body: Our first step is isolation: locating and turning the nearest isolating valve or the mains stopcock to stop active water flow and confirm the leak source. We then dry the area and run a pressure test to confirm there are no secondary leak points further along the run. For compression joint failures we disassemble the fitting, inspect the olive and nut, and re-make the joint with a new olive where necessary. For pushfit pipe systems we cut the pipe cleanly back past any deformation, re-insert the pipe insert (liner), and reconnect. Where a section of copper pipework has developed pinhole corrosion we cut out the affected length and splice in new copper or plastic using appropriate push-fit adaptors. We use epoxy repair sticks only as a temporary measure to stop active flow while parts are sourced; never as a permanent repair. All work is tested under live pressure before we leave, and we advise on any secondary damage (wet insulation, damp plasterboard) that should be allowed to dry before decoration.

sections.heading: Water Damage Risk, Timeframe, and Cost in Salisbury
sections.body: A 15mm copper pipe running at 3 bar supply pressure can release approximately 25 litres per minute through a significant failure, enough to soak a ground-floor ceiling within minutes. Even a slow drip from a compression joint loses around 30 litres per day and, over weeks, creates persistent damp that promotes mould growth in timber floor joists and plasterboard. Salisbury's large proportion of Victorian housing means many drips originate behind period panelling or within solid internal walls, making early detection important. For emergency leaks, FixWell Services aims to attend the same day across Salisbury, Amesbury, Wilton, and Downton. Our standard hourly rate is £20–£40/hr with most leak repairs completed within one to two hours once access is confirmed. Parts (olives, valves, copper fittings) are billed at cost. Acting quickly on even a minor drip is the best way to avoid a much larger repair bill for water-damaged ceilings and floors.

sections.heading: Plumbing Leaks, Emergency Response, and Wider Plumbing Repairs
sections.body: Plumbing leak repair sits within FixWell's broader plumbing repairs service, which covers the full range of minor plumbing faults, including leaking taps, running toilets, blocked drains, and appliance supply connections. Where a leak is associated with a burst pipe emergency, such as a split in a rising main following a freeze, our emergency handyman service provides the fastest route to attendance, with same-day callouts available seven days a week. Leak repair is not always a standalone job: a persistent drip at a radiator valve may indicate that the system pressure is too high, and a stopcock that weeps when operated may suggest it should be replaced before it fails completely. FixWell will advise on any related issues identified during the repair so that one visit resolves the root cause rather than just the visible symptom. For all plumbing leak repairs in Salisbury, call +44 7391 599 078 or request a quote using the form on this page.

faqs.q: How quickly can you fix a leaking pipe in Salisbury?
faqs.a: For emergency leaks (including burst pipes and active water release) we aim for same-day response across Salisbury and Wiltshire. For routine drips and weeping joints, we typically attend within one to two working days.

faqs.q: Can a slow drip really cause serious damage?
faqs.a: Yes. A drip of roughly one drop per second loses around 30 litres per day. Over weeks this saturates timber joists, softens plasterboard, and creates the damp conditions in which black mould thrives. Addressing a minor drip promptly is far cheaper than treating the secondary damage.

faqs.q: My home has old copper pipes. Can you repair them without replacing the whole run?
faqs.a: In most cases, yes. Pinhole corrosion in copper pipework is usually localised, and we can cut out the affected section and splice in a short length of new copper or plastic pipe using appropriate fittings. A full pipe replacement is only recommended when corrosion is widespread or access is severely restricted.

faqs.q: What should I do while I wait for you to arrive?
faqs.a: Turn off the nearest isolating valve for a localised leak (under the sink, behind a radiator) or your mains stopcock (usually under the kitchen sink or in the footpath inspection pit) for a burst pipe. Open a cold tap to relieve pressure, then call +44 7391 599 078. Place towels or a container to catch drips and keep the area clear of electrical fittings.

faqs.q: Do you work on pushfit plastic pipework as well as copper?
faqs.a: Yes. We work with all common pipe systems found in Salisbury homes: 15mm and 22mm copper, Speedfit/JG pushfit plastic, older polybutylene (grey plastic, 1980s–90s), and threaded steel where it survives in older properties.

faqs.q: Are you insured for plumbing work in Salisbury?
faqs.a: Yes. FixWell Services holds full public liability insurance covering all plumbing repair work we carry out. We operate within the legal handyman scope for minor plumbing. If your job requires a Gas Safe or specialist registered plumber, we will tell you clearly and can recommend a trusted local contractor.
